title: Getting On and Off: fel- and le-

sections.content: Verb prefixes attach to a plain verb to add direction. fel- means 'up/onto' and le- means 'down/off'; both combine with száll ('to board/alight') to give felszáll ('get on') and leszáll ('get off').

items.english: We get on, then you get off.

sections.content: fel- and le- are opposites you'll see again and again with other verbs too (like felpróbál 'try on'). Once you know fel- means 'up/on' and le- means 'down/off', many new verbs become easy to guess.
